questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The course opportunities, and the country was one that i really wanted to go to

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great personal experience, however the process was quite complicated

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wrote the erasmus contact person in the country, as well as the one from my home country

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not too easy, watch you that you are not being scammed

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its great

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The friends i has that lived in campus housing were not to happy with it

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to pick courses and using a tool on the website make sure that they matched timewise as well as destination wise (not having an hour travel time between courses). Then you has to register online and get it approved. It was possible to change courses which i did. The processes was not very clear, and quite confusing, i wrote the erasmus contact person many mails with questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The teachers didnt know anything about the course registration, so the helt was the erasmus conact person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: After some tries it was successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask questions, and make sure that your courses dont overlap!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine, no problem.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very monolog-oriented - the teachers were not very interactive.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Economics of Organized Crime and Corruption - Gender Justice - Society, Law and Development - Food and Environmental law - Women in Tech

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Economics of Organized Crime and Corruption - this was a very interesting and fun course. The teacher was great, and i learned a lot. The exam was nice.
Food and Environmental law - this was a great course. The food law especially. Not to much the environmental law. Again a nice exam as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike which i didnt not expect to. I didnt use it much, the traffic was insane but it was nice in the summer to have.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out was quite cheap, shopping for food was cheaper that at home but not by a shocking amount

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There werent really any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There werent really any at the university, you had to find them yourself.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
We went on a lot of trips because Milano is very well connected to the surrounding areas, this was great.
There is also an art-course every Saturday morning by Navigli right across from the market, which was amazing. 
There was the ESN-thing, but i didn´t get a lot out of it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the dolomites, to Piemonte, or to Firenze. Como was also pretty but crowded.
Crema is a beautiful little city that i would recommend visiting. Also Bergamo should be great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You have to actively talk to them, they are following the courses with their classmates, so they already have a community. When out at bars or clubs its quite straight forwards. There is no "fredagsbar" at the university, so there is not a great setting for chatting casually other then before and after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any, other then that you pay only once you have finished eating and drinking even for just a coffee, and not immediately.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the language. Everyone was very friendly. People are dressed nicely.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Have patience with the system - everything is complicated and slow. If you have to pick new courses after arrival call the student center in Denmark and talk to them about your forhåndgodkendelse - they can guide you.

Go on trips during the weekend to see the areas around Milano, they are beautiful, and many train trips only cost 5€.

Drink many aperol spritz, they are cheap and good, but watch out for the negronis, they will get you very very drunk.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Make sure that your courses align timewise and in location. Most courses have mid-terms, and some have mandatory participation, this is good to be aware of. 
The erasmus coordinator is very nice and can help you with your questions so write to him.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends, the trips and the food. Some of the courses as well.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Accepting that everything moves slower and somewhat more inefficient that at home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
